scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Route completion for 2026-08..09 was 0.88 versus a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED and 1,785 ACTUAL (3,025 total disputed bills).

F-03.statement: Dispute ticket response times for 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: Billing-db tariff change log contains 0 records.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-RESPONSE-CAPACITY.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a customer-service response-capacity/speed problem (backlog of unanswered tickets), not a rise in actual billing inaccuracy, so auto-answering tickets is the primary needed fix.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI read delivery or validation into MDMS degraded since August (vendor-side), increasing estimate substitutions and causing incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The daily manual meter-read upload from MeterWorks (ORG-FIELD) to billing degraded since August (missing/invalid reads), driving more estimate-based bills and disputes.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused more reads to be rejected or substituted with estimates, directly producing incorrect bills.

H-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: Reduced field-reading staffing/route completion since August left more meters unread, increasing estimate-based (and thus disputed) bills, as SH-FIELD attributes to staffing.

H-TARIFF-OR-CALC-ERROR.statement: A tariff rate or billing calculation error since August is producing incorrect bills even for ACTUAL meter reads, independent of estimate substitution, accounting for the majority of disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for the Aug-Sep 2026 period was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts, meaning a meaningful share of manual meter reads were missed during the dispute-surge window. This is operational evidence of a real reading shortfall, not merely a ticket-response-speed symptom.

Disputed bills split 1,785 ACTUAL vs 1,240 ESTIMATED reads (59%/41% of 3,025 total), so a majority of disputes involve bills built on actual meter reads, not estimate substitutions. This means the estimate-substitution hypotheses (AMI failure, field handoff failure, rule change, staffing) can explain at most the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes, leaving the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained.

Dispute tickets are being resolved within SLA on average and at the p90 (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA, n=2440), so the surge is not explained by a response-speed/backlog problem; this weakens the response-capacity framing that motivated the auto-answer-agent request.

The billing-db tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes are on record; this undercuts the tariff-rate-change component of H-TARIFF-OR-CALC-ERROR but does not rule out a non-tariff billing calculation error, which was proposed to explain the majority ACTUAL-read disputes (E-02).

CRM monthly dispute counts show 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul) rising to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep), confirming the surge roughly doubled starting in August as the initial request claimed. The data only establishes magnitude and timing of the surge; it does not indicate which upstream cause (response speed, estimate substitution, billing error) is responsible.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a three-reader staffing shortage since July has made routes run late, pushing affected customers onto estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim, not tool evidence, and SH-FIELD is already flagged with a staffing-attribution bias and an incentive to grow headcount, so it should be weighed as a hypothesis-supporting account rather than confirmed causation.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year, a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that corroborates the tool-derived finding (E-04) of zero tariff change log records, further undercutting any tariff-rate-change explanation for the disputed bills.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 confirms the utility may request field route priority changes but they are only executed after the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirms, matching the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update. This is an authorization document, not evidence bearing on the billing-dispute root cause.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db returned 320 accounts that received an ESTIMATED read last cycle, each tagged with an account_id and one of 40 distinct routes (E-09). This supplies the account-to-route mapping needed to pair with route-log completion data (W-WI-2A/2B), but by itself does not show which routes are lagging or confirm any causal link to the dispute surge.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 specific routes with distinct completion values (e.g. 0.70 for R-00), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 0.88 completion figure already known (E-01). This advances pending work item W-WI-2A but by itself does not yet link any lagging route to a specific disputed account, so it does not resolve whether the completion shortfall causally explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority.

U-CALC-DEFECT-LOCUS.question: Which specific billing import/validation rule or calculation step is producing incorrect bill amounts on ACTUAL-read accounts since August?
U-CALC-DEFECT-LOCUS.decision_impact: Blocks confirmation of root cause and blocks any future bill-remediation design; without it no remediation (which would require Billing Ops authority) can be proposed.

U-CALC-DEFECT-LOCUS.safe_placeholder: Treat the root cause as unconfirmed; do not propose or execute any bill remediation until the defect locus is identified via DA-RULES/DA-BILL correlation.

U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Exclude AMI-read contribution from confirmed root-cause claims and do not block diagnosis of the ACTUAL-read majority cause on this unknown.
